notes: The signalling section follows Pipe: global valid, traveling CE (cannot handle stalls, valid cleared on reset, data a don't care on reset), the simple valid and busy handshake (valid raised without waiting for busy, busy idles low, data held until the clock after the transfer), and the buffered handshake with a registered busy. That the global valid cannot stall is a fair reading of Pipe (fixed-rate data, one valid per sample); Pipe says outright only that the traveling CE cannot handle stalls.

Backpressure: combinational busy accumulating delay per stage and a registered busy costing an idle cycle or a buffer are in Pipe; the ZipCPU stall chain (op_stall, dcd_stall, pf_stall) and the two skid-buffer criteria (data constant while valid and not ready, no item lost) are in Skid. Ibex stalls its single ID/EX stage until a multi-cycle instruction finishes, and loads and stores stall at least one cycle, in the Multi- and Single-Cycle Instructions table.

Clocking: Rules says one clock, no falling-edge transitions, no rising edge of anything but the system clock, and points to enables inside clocked logic. The failure mode of a valid raised only after ready is Pipe's deadlock note.

The document's source row gives the title of the Rules post as Rules for FPGA development, for new students; the page is titled Rules for new FPGA designers. The URL is right and the content cited is there; the title in the document's front matter is inexact.
